title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
author: Arjun Pemmasani
abstract:
We prove the conjecture of Gu\'erin, Laulin, Raschel and Simon
that the bimodal initial biases of the superdiffusive elephant random walk
form a possibly empty open interval centered at one half. Outside it,
including its endpoints, the limit density has a unique local maximum.
We also prove analytically that fair-start bimodality has a unique
memory threshold. A positive-weight integral for the central curvature
reduces uniqueness to a comparison of the weights as memory increases.
Finite sign bounds pass to the limit under weak convergence and give
exactly two inflection points in the unimodal case and four in the
bimodal case. Numerical certificates locate the threshold near
$0.66881286$ and establish its quartic top. The two modes then separate
on a square-root scale, while the bias interval opens on a three-halves
scale. Above the threshold, the bias boundary
is positive and continuously differentiable, with a variational formula
and a unique optimizer. Thus strongly biased starts are unimodal at
every fixed memory, although the boundary tends to zero as memory
tends to one.
